questions.question: A number is doubled and then reduced by 12, resulting in 28. What was the original number?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Final value = 28

Operations: Number is **doubled** and then **reduced by 12**.

**Formula Used:**

Linear Equation: 2x − 12 = 28

Let the **original number** be x.

According to the problem statement:

⇒ 2 × x − 12 = 28

⇒ 2x = 28 + 12

⇒ 2x = 40

⇒ x = 40 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

questions.question: Which Indian leader received France's highest civilian award, the Legion of Honour, in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narendra Modi**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** was conferred with the **Grand Cross of the Legion of Honour**, which is the highest civilian and military honor of **France**, in July **2023**.

• The award was presented to him by the French President **Emmanuel Macron** at the **Elysee Palace** in Paris.

• PM Modi became the **first Indian Prime Minister** to receive this prestigious award.

• The honor was bestowed during his two-day official visit to France, where he attended the **Bastille Day Parade** as the **Guest of Honour**.

• This recognition highlights the strengthening of the **strategic partnership** between India and France and acknowledges the Prime Minister's role in enhancing bilateral ties.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Legion of Honour** (Ordre national de la Légion d'honneur) was established by **Napoleon Bonaparte** in **1802**.

• It is the highest French order of merit, both military and civil, and is divided into five degrees: **Knight**, **Officer**, **Commander**, **Grand Officer**, and **Grand Cross**.

• The **Grand Cross** is the highest level within the order.

• Other notable international leaders who have received the Grand Cross include **Nelson Mandela**, **King Charles III**, and **Angela Merkel**.

• In 2023, PM Modi also received several other top international honors, including the **Order of the Nile** (Egypt) and the **Grand Companion of the Order of Logohu** (Papua New Guinea).

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which of the following is correct regarding the punishment for mob lynching?

options.text: Only imprisonment up to 5 years is allowed
Punishable with up to 7 years, life imprisonment, or death
Mob lynching is treated as a bailable offence with a fine
Only life imprisonment is prescribed regardless of severity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punishable with up to 7 years, life imprisonment, or death**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023**, which replaces the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)**, has introduced specific provisions to deal with the offence of **mob lynching**.

• Under **Section 103(2)** of the BNS, when a group of **five or more persons** acting in concert commits murder on the ground of **race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief** or any other similar ground, each member of such group shall be punished.

• The prescribed punishment for this offence includes **death**, **imprisonment for life**, or **imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years**, and the offenders shall also be liable to a **fine**.

• This provision was specifically added to provide a legal framework to penalize **hate-motivated killings** by mobs, which was not explicitly defined as a separate category under the old IPC.

• Other options are incorrect because the law provides for a range of punishments depending on the severity, including the **death penalty**, and it is categorized as a **heinous, non-bailable offence**.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)** received the President's assent on **December 25, 2023**, and officially came into force on **July 1, 2024**.

• Along with the BNS, two other major laws were enacted: the **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, replacing the CrPC, and the **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)**, replacing the Indian Evidence Act.

• The introduction of **Section 103(2)** follows various directives from the **Supreme Court of India** (notably in the **Tehseen Poonawalla case**) urging the government to create a special law to tackle lynching.

• The BNS also introduces other new categories of offences such as **organized crime** and **terrorist acts** within the general penal code.
</ul

questions.question: What is the primary source of energy driving the water cycle on Earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solar energy**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **water cycle**, also known as the **hydrologic cycle**, describes the continuous movement of water on, above, and below the surface of the Earth.

• **Solar energy** (energy from the **Sun**) is the primary driver of this cycle because it provides the heat necessary for **evaporation** and **transpiration**.

• When the Sun heats the water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, it changes from a liquid state to a gaseous state called **water vapor**, which rises into the atmosphere.

• **Geothermal energy** comes from the internal heat of the Earth and, while it can influence local water systems like hot springs, it is not the primary driver of the global water cycle.

• **Wind energy** is actually a byproduct of uneven solar heating of the atmosphere; while it helps transport moisture, it is not the original source of energy for the cycle.

• **Ocean tides** are primarily caused by the **gravitational pull** of the Moon and the Sun and involve the physical movement of water bodies rather than the cycle of evaporation and precipitation.

**Additional Information__**

• The water cycle involves several key processes: **evaporation**, **condensation** (forming clouds), **precipitation** (rain, snow, hail), **infiltration** (water soaking into the ground), and **runoff**.

• **Gravity** plays a crucial secondary role in the water cycle by pulling precipitation down to the surface and causing water to flow from higher elevations to lower elevations in rivers and streams.

• Approximately 97 percent of Earth's water is stored in the **oceans**, which serve as the largest reservoir for the evaporation process driven by the Sun.

• **Sublimation** is another part of the cycle where ice and snow turn directly into water vapor without melting into liquid first, also powered by solar radiation.
</ul

questions.question: Why is the management of subsurface fluid reservoir important?

options.text: For both economic and environmental reasons
For neither economic nor environmental reasons

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**For both economic and environmental reasons**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The management of **subsurface fluid reservoirs** (which include oil, natural gas, groundwater, and geothermal fluids) is a multidisciplinary task that addresses both **financial viability** and **ecological safety**.

• **Economic Importance:** Reservoirs are significant **natural assets**. Effective management involves optimizing the **extraction rate** and **recovery factor** to ensure that resources are not wasted. This maximizes the **revenue** for industries and governments while ensuring energy and water security.

• **Environmental Importance:** Subsurface activities can have significant footprints. Proper management prevents **aquifer contamination**, **surface leakage** of hazardous fluids, and **land subsidence**. It is also vital for **Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)**, where CO2 is injected into reservoirs to mitigate **global warming**.

• Options (1) and (2) are considered **reductive** because they ignore the interconnected nature of industrial operations and environmental stewardship. Option (4) is incorrect as it dismisses the two primary drivers of modern **georesource engineering**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Induced Seismicity:** Improper fluid injection or extraction in subsurface reservoirs can lead to **artificial earthquakes**, making monitoring and management a public safety priority.

• **Sustainable Development:** The **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** emphasize the responsible use of underground resources to balance **economic growth** with **environmental protection**.

• **Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR):** This management technique uses **gas injection** or **chemical flooding** to extract oil that cannot be recovered through primary or secondary means, showcasing the economic drive behind reservoir management.

• **Hydrogeology:** In the context of **water reservoirs**, management is crucial to prevent **saltwater intrusion** in coastal regions, which can permanently damage freshwater supplies.
</ul

questions.question: What is another use of bleaching powder besides bleaching?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Disinfecting drinking water**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• **Bleaching powder**, chemically known as **Calcium Oxychloride** (CaOCl₂), is extensively used as a **disinfectant** for drinking water to make it free from **germs** and **pathogens**.

• When bleaching powder is added to water, it releases **chlorine**, which acts as a powerful **germicide** that kills bacteria and other microorganisms, ensuring the water is safe for consumption.

• **Making soap** and **making detergent** primarily involve the process of **saponification**, which uses fats or oils and strong alkalis like **Sodium Hydroxide** (NaOH) or **Potassium Hydroxide** (KOH), rather than bleaching powder.

• **Making paint** involves pigments, binders, and solvents; bleaching powder is not a standard ingredient in the manufacturing of paint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Bleaching powder is produced by the action of **chlorine gas** on **dry slaked lime** [Ca(OH)₂].

• It is used as a strong **oxidizing agent** in many chemical industries due to its ability to release oxygen.

• In the **textile industry**, it is used for bleaching **cotton** and **linen**, and in the **paper industry**, it is used for bleaching **wood pulp**.

• It is also used for **bleaching washed clothes** in laundries and for the **unshrinkable** treatment of wool.

• Bleaching powder should be stored in a cool, dry place because it loses its **chlorine content** when exposed to air or moisture.

questions.question: Which of the following is a direct tax collected by the government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Income Tax**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Income Tax** is a **direct tax** because it is levied directly on the **income** of **individuals**, **Hindu Undivided Families (HUF)**, and other **legal entities**. The **taxpayer** pays this tax directly to the **government**, and the **tax burden** cannot be shifted to another person. ***Hence, the correct answer is Income Tax.***

• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is an **indirect tax** that was introduced to replace multiple **indirect taxes** like **VAT** and **Service Tax**. It is collected by the **seller** from the **buyer** and then deposited with the **government**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Customs Duty** is an **indirect tax** imposed on **goods** that are **imported** into or **exported** out of **India**. It is generally passed on to the **final consumer** as part of the **product price**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• **Excise Duty** is an **indirect tax** levied on the **manufacture** or **production** of goods within the **country**. While most **excise duties** are now subsumed under **GST**, it still applies to items like **petroleum** and **liquor**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

• A **direct tax** is characterized by the fact that the **incidence** and **impact** of the tax fall on the same **individual** or **entity**, making it a **non-transferable** liability.

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Income Tax Act, 1961** is the **primary legislation** governing the **levy** and **collection** of **income tax** in **India**. It is updated every **year** through the **Finance Act** during the **Union Budget**.

• The **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)** is the **statutory authority** responsible for the **administration** of **direct tax laws**. It functions under the **Department of Revenue** in the **Ministry of Finance**.

• **Indirect taxes** in **India** are managed by the **Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)**. **GST** was implemented on **1st July 2017** through the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act**.

• **Direct taxes** are **progressive** in nature, meaning the **tax rate** increases as the **taxable income** of the **taxpayer** increases, which helps in reducing **income inequality**.

• **Indirect taxes** are considered **regressive** because they are applied at the same **rate** to all **consumers**, regardless of their **income level** or **wealth**.

**Important Points__**

• **Corporate Tax** is another major **direct tax** levied on the **net profits** earned by **domestic** and **foreign companies** from their **operations** in **India**.

• **Wealth Tax** was a **direct tax** on the **net wealth** of **individuals**, but it was **abolished** in the **year 2015** to simplify the **tax structure** and reduce **administrative costs**.

• **Capital Gains Tax** is a **direct tax** charged on the **profits** made from the **sale** of **capital assets** such as **real estate**, **stocks**, and **bonds**. It is divided into **Short-Term** and **Long-Term Capital Gains**.

• **Securities Transaction Tax (STT)** is a **direct tax** levied on the **value** of **taxable securities** transactions done through a **recognized stock exchange** in **India**.
</ul

questions.question: In basketball, a player must release the ball within how many seconds when attempting a free throw?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10 seconds**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Official Basketball Rules** established by **FIBA** (International Basketball Federation) and the **NBA** (National Basketball Association), a player must release the ball within **10 seconds** when attempting a **free throw**.
 
• The **10-second count** begins as soon as the **official** or **referee** places the ball at the **disposal** of the shooter at the **free-throw line**.
 
• If the player fails to release the ball within this **time limit**, a **violation** is called. This results in the **cancellation** of the shot (if it goes in) and the ball being awarded to the **opposing team** for a **throw-in** from the **sideline**, provided no further free throws are pending.
 
• This rule is designed to maintain the **pace of the game** and prevent players from using the **free-throw line** as an opportunity for excessive **rest** or **stalling**.
 
• The option of **5 seconds** is incorrect for free throws; however, it is a critical **numerical value** used for **inbounding** the ball or when a player is **closely guarded** in the frontcourt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which metal is primarily used to make Olympic gold medals?

The correct answer is __**Silver**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• Olympic gold medals are primarily made of **Silver**, not solid gold. According to the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** guidelines, the gold medal must be composed of at least **92.5% silver** (Sterling Silver). *Hence, the correct answer is Silver.*

• The medal is finished with a plating of at least **6 grams of pure gold** to give it its characteristic appearance. **Gold** is used only as a thin outer layer because a solid gold medal would be prohibitively expensive and too soft to maintain its detailed engravings. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

• **Silver** provides the necessary **structural integrity** and **durability** for the medal. It is also the primary component of the **second-place** medals, which are made of the same **92.5% silver** grade but without the gold gilding.

• **Bronze** and **Copper** are the primary materials used for the **third-place** medals. A bronze medal typically consists of **95% to 97% copper** mixed with **zinc** or **tin**. *Hence, statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.*

• The **composition** of Olympic medals has evolved over time to balance **prestige**, **cost**, and **material science**, ensuring that the medals remain a symbol of excellence while being practical to produce in large quantities for the **Summer** and **Winter Games**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Historical Evolution:** The last time **solid gold medals** were awarded was at the **1912 Stockholm Olympics**. Since then, the **silver-gilt** standard has been adopted globally for all subsequent **Olympic Games**.

• **Tokyo 2020 Sustainability:** For the **2020 Tokyo Olympics**, the **Organizing Committee** launched the **Tokyo 2020 Medal Project**, where medals were crafted entirely from **recycled metals** extracted from nearly **79,000 tons** of discarded electronic devices, including **6.21 million mobile phones**.

• **Paris 2024 Unique Feature:** The medals for the **Paris 2024 Olympics** included a piece of **original iron** from the **Eiffel Tower**. This **18-gram** hexagonal piece was placed in the center of the medals to link the athletes with the **heritage of France**.

• **Monetary Value:** While the **sentimental value** is priceless, the **melt value** of a gold medal is significantly lower than its appearance suggests. As of **2024**, the raw metal value of a gold medal is roughly **$900 to $1,000**, whereas a solid gold version would exceed **$40,000**.

• **Design Standards:** The **obverse side** of the medals traditionally features **Nike**, the Greek goddess of victory, flying into the **Panathenaic Stadium** in **Athens**, a design that has been mandatory since the **2004 Athens Games**.

**Important Points__**

• **IOC Regulations:** The **Olympic Charter** specifies that medals must be at least **60mm in diameter** and **3mm thick**. Modern medals are often larger, typically around **85mm** in diameter and **8-10mm** thick.

• **Weight Variations:** A standard Olympic gold medal weighs between **500 and 580 grams**. The **Silver** medal weighs approximately **550 grams**, and the **Bronze** medal weighs about **450 grams**.

• **Manufacturing Process:** The medals are produced by the **National Mint** of the host country. For example, the **United States Mint**, **Royal Mint (UK)**, or **China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation** have handled production for their respective games.

• **Host City Customization:** While the **front** of the medal is largely standardized by the **IOC**, the **reverse side** is designed by the **host city** to showcase their **culture**, **art**, and **national identity**.

questions.question: A high Ease of Doing Business (EODB) score means it is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Easy to start a business**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Ease of Doing Business (EODB)** index is a ranking system created by the **World Bank Group** to measure how conducive the regulatory environment of a country is to the starting and operation of a local firm. A high **EODB** score (closer to **100**) or a low numerical rank (e.g., **1st**, **2nd**) indicates that it is **Easy to start a business** due to streamlined processes and efficient regulations. ***Hence, the statement 'Easy to start a business' is correct.***

• A high score signifies that the government has implemented **simpler regulations** for businesses and **stronger protections of property rights**, which encourages entrepreneurship and economic activity. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***

• If a country has a low score or a poor ranking, it implies that the regulatory environment is burdensome, making it **Hard to start a business** due to excessive red tape, high costs, or lengthy administrative procedures. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• The **EODB** index specifically focuses on business and commercial regulations; it does not measure the **cost of travel** or tourism-related expenses. Therefore, a high score does not mean it is **Expensive to travel**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• While a better business environment typically leads to more investment and job creation, the **EODB** score is not a direct metric for the labor market's difficulty or the ease of a personal job search. Thus, it does not mean it is **Difficult to find a job**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Doing Business** project was first launched in **2003**. It provided objective measures of business regulations and their enforcement across **190 economies** and selected cities at the subnational and regional levels.

• The index was calculated based on **10 to 12 indicators**, including **Starting a Business**, **Dealing with Construction Permits**, **Getting Electricity**, **Registering Property**, **Getting Credit**, **Protecting Minority Investors**, **Paying Taxes**, **Trading across Borders**, **Enforcing Contracts**, and **Resolving Insolvency**.

• **India** showed a remarkable trajectory in these rankings, moving from **142nd position in 2014** to **63rd position in 2020**. This improvement was attributed to initiatives like **Make in India**, the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) 2016**, and the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**.

• In **September 2021**, the **World Bank** decided to discontinue the **Doing Business** report following internal audits that revealed data irregularities in previous reports (specifically for the **2018** and **2020** editions).

• The **World Bank** has since replaced the **EODB** with a new flagship series called **Business Ready (B-READY)**, which aims to provide a more holistic and transparent assessment of the business and investment climate worldwide.

**Important Points__**

• The **Starting a Business** indicator specifically tracks the number of procedures, time, cost, and paid-in minimum capital required for a small-to-medium-sized limited liability company to formally operate.

• A high **EODB** score is a critical factor for attracting **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, as international investors prioritize countries with transparent **legal frameworks** and efficient **administrative systems**.

• In **India**, the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**, under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, is the nodal agency that drives reforms to improve the business environment at both the **National** and **State** levels through the **State Reform Action Plan (SRAP)**.

• For the purpose of the **World Bank** rankings in **India**, data was primarily collected from the business environments of **Delhi** and **Mumbai**, representing the country's major commercial hubs.
</ul

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey (1757) marked the beginning of British rule in India. Which earlier battle marked the decline of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Battle of Panipat (1526)**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **First Battle of Panipat**, fought on **21 April 1526**, is the landmark event that marked the end of the **Delhi Sultanate** and the beginning of the **Mughal Empire** in India. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• The battle was fought between the invading forces of **Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur** and the **Lodi Dynasty** led by **Ibrahim Lodi**. **Ibrahim Lodi** was the last Sultan of the **Delhi Sultanate**, and his death on the battlefield signified the total collapse of the Sultanate rule that had lasted since **1206**.

• The **Battle of Talikota (1565)** was a watershed battle fought between the **Vijayanagara Empire** and the **Deccan Sultanates** (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, and Bidar). This battle led to the decline of the **Vijayanagara Empire** in South India, not the Delhi Sultanate. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **Battle of Khanwa (1527)** took place a year after the fall of the Delhi Sultanate. It was fought between **Babur** and the **Rajput** forces led by **Rana Sanga** of **Mewar**. This battle consolidated **Mughal** power but did not mark the decline of the Sultanate as it had already ceased to exist. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• The **Battle of Tarain (1192)**, specifically the **Second Battle of Tarain**, saw **Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad Ghori** defeat **Prithviraj Chauhan**. This event is historically recognized as the **establishment** and **foundation** of Muslim rule and the **Delhi Sultanate** in India, rather than its decline. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **The Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526):** The Sultanate era spanned over **three centuries** and was characterized by five successive dynasties: the **Mamluk (Slave) Dynasty**, the **Khalji Dynasty**, the **Tughlaq Dynasty**, the **Sayyid Dynasty**, and the **Lodi Dynasty**. The **Lodi Dynasty** was the final phase, ending with **Ibrahim Lodi**.

• **Military Innovation at Panipat:** **Babur** was able to defeat a much larger army of **Ibrahim Lodi** (estimated at **100,000 soldiers** and **1,000 elephants**) primarily due to his use of **field artillery** and **gunpowder firearms**, which were relatively new to **Northern India** at the time. He employed the **Tulughma** (encirclement) tactic and the **Araba** (carts tied together to protect artillery) system.

• **The Role of Invitations:** **Babur**, the ruler of **Kabul**, was invited to invade India by **Daulat Khan Lodi** (the Governor of **Punjab**) and **Alam Khan** (uncle of Ibrahim Lodi), who were dissatisfied with **Ibrahim Lodi’s** tyrannical rule.

• **The Battle of Plassey (1757):** Fought on **23 June 1757**, this battle saw the **British East India Company**, led by **Robert Clive**, defeat the **Nawab of Bengal**, **Siraj-ud-Daulah**. It is considered the starting point of **British Colonial rule** in India, much like Panipat started the **Mughal** era.

• **Successive Panipat Battles:** The **Second Battle of Panipat (1556)** was fought between **Akbar** and **Hemu**, securing the Mughal throne. The **Third Battle of Panipat (1761)** was fought between the **Maratha Empire** and the **Afghan** invader **Ahmad Shah Abdali**, which weakened Maratha power and indirectly aided British expansion.

**Important Points__**

• **Ibrahim Lodi** holds the distinction of being the only **Sultan of Delhi** to have been killed on the **battlefield**.

• The **Lodi Dynasty** was of **Afghan** origin, founded by **Bahlul Lodi** in **1451**, following the decline of the **Sayyid Dynasty**.

• The transition from the **Delhi Sultanate** to the **Mughal Empire** shifted the political center of gravity and introduced a new era of **Indo-Islamic architecture** and **administrative reforms** that peaked under **Akbar**.

• While the **Battle of Panipat** ended the Sultanate, the **Battle of Buxar (1764)** is often cited alongside the **Battle of Plassey** as the final seal on **British political authority** over the **Mughal Emperor** and the **Nawab of Awadh**.

questions.question: The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was fought between which two leaders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar and Rana Pratap**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Battle of Haldighati** was a significant historical conflict fought on **June 18, 1576**. It took place between the forces of the **Mughal Emperor Akbar** and the **Rajput** king of **Mewar**, **Maharana Pratap**. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*

• The **Mughal** army was led by **Raja Man Singh I** of **Amber**, who was one of **Akbar**'s most trusted generals. On the other side, **Maharana Pratap** led the **Mewar** forces, defending his kingdom's sovereignty against **Mughal** expansion.

• The battle occurred at **Haldighati**, a narrow mountain pass in the **Aravalli Range** near **Gogunda** in **Rajasthan**. The name **Haldighati** is derived from the turmeric-colored (yellow) soil of the region.

• While the **Mughal** forces technically won the battle by occupying the ground, they failed to capture **Maharana Pratap**. **Pratap** managed to escape to the hills, from where he continued a long-term **guerrilla warfare** against the **Mughal Empire**.

• Regarding the other options: The **Battle of Khanwa** in **1527** was fought between **Babur and Rana Sanga**. The **Battle of Chausa (1539)** and **Battle of Kannauj (1540)** were fought between **Sher Shah Suri and Humayun**. **Jahangir and Rana Amar Singh** (son of Pratap) eventually ended the long-standing conflict through a peace treaty in **1615**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Maharana Pratap (1540–1597):** He was the **13th King of Mewar** and is celebrated as a national hero in **India** for his bravery and refusal to submit to the **Mughal** authority. He spent much of his life in the **Aravalli** mountains, organizing resistance.

• **Chetak:** This was the name of **Maharana Pratap**'s legendary horse. During the **Battle of Haldighati**, **Chetak** is said to have carried his master to safety despite being severely injured, eventually collapsing and dying. A memorial for **Chetak** stands at **Haldighati** today.

• **Hakim Khan Suri:** Interestingly, the vanguard of **Maharana Pratap**'s army was led by an **Afghan** general named **Hakim Khan Suri**, showing that the battle was a political struggle for independence rather than a purely religious one.

• **Raja Man Singh I:** He was the **Kachwaha Rajput** King of **Amber** and a primary commander in the **Mughal** army. His leadership at **Haldighati** represented **Akbar**'s policy of incorporating **Rajput** rulers into the **Mughal** administrative and military hierarchy.

• **Guerrilla Warfare:** After the battle, **Maharana Pratap** utilized the difficult terrain of the **Aravallis** to conduct **guerrilla tactics**. By the time of his death in **1597**, he had successfully recovered most of his ancestral territories, including **Udaipur** and **Kumbhalgarh**, though **Chittorgarh** remained under **Mughal** control.

**Important Points__**

• **Strength of Forces:** Historical accounts vary, but it is generally accepted that the **Mughal** army significantly outnumbered the **Mewar** forces. The **Mughals** had approximately **5,000 to 10,000** soldiers, while **Pratap** had around **3,000** horsemen and **400 Bhil** archers.

• **Bhil Community:** The local **Bhil** tribes played a crucial role in supporting **Maharana Pratap**. Their expertise in the hilly terrain and **archery** was vital for the **Rajput** resistance during and after the battle.

• **Historical Significance:** The **Battle of Haldighati** is often cited as a classic example of a smaller force using **geography** and **valor** to withstand a much larger imperial power, cementing **Maharana Pratap**'s legacy in **Indian** folklore.

questions.question: The Amarkantak Plateau region has which of the following river flowing through it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Narmada River** originates from the **Narmada Kund** located on the **Amarkantak Plateau** in the **Anuppur district** of **Madhya Pradesh**. It is the most significant river that flows through this plateau region. *Hence, this option is correct.*

• The **Godavari River** has its origin at **Trimbakeshwar** in the **Nashik district** of **Maharashtra**. It flows across the **Deccan Plateau** toward the east and does not pass through the **Amarkantak** region. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

• The **Krishna River** originates near **Mahabaleshwar** in the **Western Ghats** of **Maharashtra**. Its course takes it through the states of **Karnataka**, **Telangana**, and **Andhra Pradesh**, which is geographically distant from the **Amarkantak Plateau**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

• The **Ganga River** originates from the **Gangotri Glacier** at **Gaumukh** in the **Uttarkashi district** of **Uttarakhand**. It flows through the northern **Indo-Gangetic plains** and does not pass through the **Amarkantak Plateau**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Amarkantak** is a unique natural heritage area and is the meeting point of the **Vindhya Range** and the **Satpura Range**, specifically within the **Maikal Hills**. It is often referred to as **'Teerthraj'** (the king of pilgrimages) and sits at an altitude of approximately **1,048 meters**.

• The **Narmada River** is the largest **west-flowing river** in Peninsular India, covering a total distance of about **1,312 km** before emptying into the **Arabian Sea** through the **Gulf of Khambhat**.

• Unlike most peninsular rivers that flow east into the Bay of Bengal, the **Narmada** flows west because it occupies a **Rift Valley** formed by the downward faulting of the land between the **Vindhya** and **Satpura** ranges.

• Apart from the **Narmada**, the **Son River** also originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau**. It flows north-northeast to join the **Ganga** as one of its major southern tributaries.

• The **Johila River** is another stream that takes its birth in the **Amarkantak** hills and eventually joins the **Son River**.

**Important Points__**

• The **Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve** was established in **2005** and was later included in the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves** in **2012** to protect the rich biodiversity of the region.

• The **Narmada River** is considered one of the seven holy rivers of India and is known as the **'Life Line of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat'** due to its vital role in irrigation, drinking water, and power generation.

• Famous landmarks along the river include the **Dhuandhar Falls** in **Jabalpur**, where the river plunges over **Marble Rocks**, and the **Sardar Sarovar Dam** in **Gujarat**, which is one of the largest dams in the world.

• Other significant hydroelectric projects on the river include the **Indira Sagar Dam** and the **Omkareshwar Dam**, both located in **Madhya Pradesh**.

questions.question: What was the primary reason for introducing economic reforms in India in 1991?
questions.solution:
p The correct answer is __**Balance of payments crisis**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The primary reason for introducing economic reforms in **1991** was the severe **Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis**. India faced a situation where its foreign exchange reserves had depleted to approximately **$1.2 billion**, which was barely sufficient to pay for **two weeks** of essential imports like **crude oil**. **Hence, option 2 is correct.**

• The **fiscal deficit** of the government had reached a high of **8.4%** of the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** in **1990-91**, leading to a massive internal debt trap and high **inflation** rates, which peaked at around **16.7%** in **August 1991**.

• The **Gulf War** of **1990-91** exacerbated the situation by causing a sharp spike in **petroleum prices** and a significant reduction in **remittances** from Indian workers living in the Gulf region.

• The option **High GDP growth** is incorrect because, during the late **1980s** and early **1990s**, the economy was struggling with inefficiency, and the growth was unsustainable due to heavy external borrowing. **Hence, option 1 is incorrect.**

• While **Overpopulation** and **Agricultural stagnation** were long-term structural challenges for the Indian economy, they were not the immediate triggers for the emergency policy shift in **1991**. The reforms were a response to the imminent threat of defaulting on international sovereign debt. **Hence, options 3 and 4 are incorrect.**

**Additional Information__**

__

• The **New Economic Policy (NEP)** was formally launched on **July 24, 1991**, under the leadership of Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and the then Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**.

• The reforms are widely known as the **LPG Model**, which stands for **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization**. This marked the end of the **License Permit Raj**, which had restricted private sector growth for decades.

• **Liberalization** involved the removal of government regulations and barriers to entry for private businesses, allowing for **market-driven** competition. It included the abolition of **industrial licensing** for most industries.

• **Privatization** referred to the process of **disinvestment**, where the government sold its shares in **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** to private investors to improve operational efficiency and reduce the fiscal burden.

• **Globalization** aimed at integrating the Indian economy with the global market by reducing **import tariffs**, encouraging **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, and allowing the **Indian Rupee** to be determined by market forces (partial convertibility).

• To manage the immediate crisis in **1991**, India had to pledge its **gold reserves**. Approximately **47 tonnes** of gold were shipped to the **Bank of England** and **20 tonnes** to the **Union Bank of Switzerland** to secure a loan of **$600 million**.

**Important Points__**

• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Bank** provided a bailout package of **$7 billion** to India, but it came with strict conditions for **structural adjustment** and economic stabilization.

• The **Rupee** was devalued twice in **July 1991** (by about **18-20%**) to make Indian exports more competitive and to discourage imports, thereby helping to stabilize the **Balance of Payments**.

• The **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act** was amended to remove the threshold limit of assets, allowing large companies to expand without prior government approval, further boosting industrial growth.

questions.question: What is the supreme law of India?
questions.solution:
pThe correct answer is __**Indian Constitution**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Indian Constitution** is the **supreme law of India** because it establishes the framework that defines fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.

• All laws enacted by the **Parliament** or state legislatures, and all executive actions taken by the **President** or Governors, must be in conformity with the **Constitution**. If any law violates the provisions of the Constitution, the **Judiciary** has the power to declare it null and void.

• The **Supreme Court Judgment** is considered the law of the land under **Article 141**, but it is an interpretation of the law and the Constitution, not the supreme law itself. Judgments must align with constitutional mandates. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• The **Parliament** of India is the supreme legislative body, but its powers are derived from and limited by the **Constitution**. It cannot pass laws that override the **Basic Structure** of the Constitution as defined in the **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973)**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **Indian Constitution** was adopted by the **Constituent Assembly** on **26 November 1949** and became effective on **26 January 1950**. It imparts **constitutional supremacy** rather than parliamentary supremacy. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• A **President's Order** (such as an **Ordinance** under **Article 123**) has the same force as an Act of Parliament but is temporary and subject to the **Constitution** and judicial review. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Constitution of India** is the **longest written constitution** of any sovereign country in the world, originally containing **395 Articles** in **22 Parts** and **8 Schedules**.

• Currently, after various amendments, it has approximately **448 Articles** grouped into **25 Parts** and **12 Schedules**.

• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, the Chairman of the **Drafting Committee**, is widely regarded as the **Chief Architect** or the **Father of the Indian Constitution**.

• The **Preamble** of the Constitution declares India to be a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, and Democratic Republic**, ensuring justice, liberty, and equality to all its citizens.

• The **Constitution** was not printed but **calligraphed** in both **Hindi** and **English** by **Prem Behari Narain Raizada**.

• The **Constituent Assembly** took exactly **2 years, 11 months, and 18 days** to complete the final draft of the **Constitution**.

**Important Points__**

• **Article 13**: This article explicitly provides for the doctrine of **Judicial Review**. It states that all laws in force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of the Constitution, in so far as they are inconsistent with the provisions of **Fundamental Rights (Part III)**, shall be void.

• **Basic Structure Doctrine**: Established by the **Supreme Court** in **1973**, this doctrine prevents the **Parliament** from using its amendment powers under **Article 368** to alter the essential features of the **Constitution**, such as **Secularism**, **Federalism**, and **Democracy**.

• **Constitutional Supremacy vs. Parliamentary Supremacy**: Unlike the **United Kingdom**, where **Parliament** is supreme, India follows **Constitutional Supremacy**, where the **Constitution** is the highest legal authority.

• **Emergency Provisions**: Under **Articles 352, 356, and 360**, the **Constitution** provides for the suspension of certain rights and the shifting of the federal structure to a unitary one, yet even these actions must follow the **Constitutional** procedure.
</ul

questions.question: If x = 7/2 is a rational number and y = sqrt{27} , an irrational number, then x + y is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Property: The sum of a **rational number** and an **irrational number** is always an **irrational number**.

Given: x = 7/2 (Rational) and y = √27 (Irrational).

Logic: Rational + Irrational → **Irrational**.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x = 7/2 = 3.5 (A **rational number** with a terminating decimal expansion)

y = √27 = √(9 × 3) = 3√3 (An **irrational number** with a non-terminating, non-recurring decimal expansion)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/652d0710c1bb112e3cacceee22ad0a9c54296de59715c39bc5eb025c06770d70.png] 

⇒ x = 3.5

⇒ y = 3 × 1.7320508...

⇒ y ≈ 5.1961524...

⇒ x + y = 3.5 + 5.1961524...

⇒ x + y = 8.6961524...

Since the sum results in a decimal expansion that is **non-terminating** and **non-recurring**, the resulting number is **irrational**.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Rational and Irrational

The product of a **non-zero rational number** and an **irrational number** is always **irrational**.

Sum of two Irrational Numbers

The sum of two irrational numbers is **not always irrational**; it can be rational (e.g., √2 + (−√2) = 0).

Rational Number Definition

A number that can be expressed in the form **p/q** where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.

questions.question: If a number is rational, it cannot be:

Rational and Irrational numbers are **mutually exclusive** sets.

A number can either be expressed as a fraction p/q (Rational) or it cannot (Irrational).

Natural numbers, Whole numbers, and Integers are all **subsets** of Rational numbers.

Since a number cannot belong to both sets simultaneously, a rational number can never be irrational.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A number is rational.

**Definition:** A rational number is any number that can be written in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f73e7e8ead91b0dde2dd850338ab651e6b36476d8db7081773b142cf8223e1a.png] 

⇒ **Natural numbers** (1, 2, 3...) can be written as 1/1, 2/1, 3/1 (Rational).

⇒ **Whole numbers** (0, 1, 2...) can be written as 0/1, 1/1, 2/1 (Rational).

⇒ **Integers** (...−2, −1, 0, 1, 2...) can be written as −2/1, −1/1 (Rational).

⇒ **Irrational numbers** are those that cannot be expressed as p/q (e.g., √2, π).

⇒ If a number is in the Rational set, it is physically impossible for it to be in the Irrational set.

**∴ The correct answer is Irrational.**

Real Number System

Real numbers are divided into two distinct groups: Rational and Irrational. Their intersection is an empty set.

Decimal Representation

Rational numbers have decimals that either **terminate** (e.g., 0.5) or **repeat** (e.g., 0.333...). Irrational numbers have **non-terminating** and **non-repeating** decimals.

Subsets of Rational Numbers

The hierarchy is: Natural Numbers ⊂ Whole Numbers ⊂ Integers ⊂ Rational Numbers.</p

questions.question:
What will be the number of zeros at the end of the square of the following numbers?
(i) 70
(ii) 500
Choose the correct option:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The number of zeros at the end of a square is always double the number of zeros in the original number.

(i) 70 ends in 1 zero → 70² ends in 1 × 2 = 2 zeros.

(ii) 500 ends in 2 zeros → 500² ends in 2 × 2 = 4 zeros.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 zeros in (i), 4 zeros in (ii).**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers (i) 70 and (ii) 500.

**Formula Used:** (a × 10ⁿ)² = a² × 10²ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2cbedf2a986fbaceed4c8466b465b8c23d578afed555b1bb5ca95701ceac84d.png] 

⇒ For (i) 70: 70² = 70 × 70 = 4900

⇒ Number of zeros at the end of 4900 = 2

⇒ For (ii) 500: 500² = 500 × 500 = 250000

⇒ Number of zeros at the end of 250000 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 2 zeros in (i), 4 zeros in (ii).**

**__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Trailing Zeros

A perfect square always ends with an even number of zeros. If a number ends in an odd number of zeros, it cannot be a perfect square.

Zeros in Cubes

If a number ends in n zeros, its cube will end in 3 × n zeros. For example, 10³ = 1000 (3 zeros).

Unit Digit Rule

The square of any number can only end in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9. It can never end in 2, 3, 7, or 8.</p

questions.question: If ₹1,200 earns ₹216 as interest in 3 years, what is the rate of interest?

**Rate (R)** = (**Simple Interest** × 100) ÷ (**Principal** × **Time**)

**Rate** = (216 × 100) ÷ (1200 × 3)

**Rate** = 216 ÷ 36 = 6%

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,200

**Interest (I)** = ₹216

**Time (T)** = 3 years

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Simple Interest** for 3 years = ₹216

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 1 year = 216 ÷ 3 = ₹72

⇒ **Rate of Interest (R)** = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100

⇒ **R** = (72 ÷ 1200) × 100

⇒ **R** = 72 ÷ 12 = 6%

**∴ The correct answer is 6%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

The interest remains constant every year and is calculated as SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

Amount is the sum of the **Principal** and the **Simple Interest**: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Rate and Time Relation

For a fixed **Principal**, the **Interest** is directly proportional to both the **Rate** and the **Time**.

questions.question: In a pair of concentric circles, a chord drawn in the larger circle just touches the smaller circle at a single point Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The chord is always longer than the radius of the smaller circle.
The chord is bisected at the point where it touches the smaller circle.
The chord lies entirely outside the smaller circle.
The chord passes through the center of both circles.

questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A tangent to the inner circle is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

For the larger circle, this radius acts as a perpendicular from the center to the chord.

The perpendicular from the center of a circle to a chord always bisects the chord.

**∴ The correct answer is The chord is bisected at the point where it touches the smaller circle.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two concentric circles with center O. AB is a chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle at point P.

**Formula Used:** 1. Tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. 2. Perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8cd7608aa118887760a1036e1d48b7a7e4400fdc92b9ddb3c94c8ebe179e1aa0.png] 

⇒ Let the radius of the smaller circle be OP.

⇒ Since AB is a tangent to the smaller circle at P, OP ⊥ AB.

⇒ For the larger circle, AB is a chord and OP is the perpendicular from the center O to the chord AB.

⇒ According to the circle theorem, the perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord.

⇒ ∴ AP = PB.

**∴ The correct answer is The chord is bisected at the point where it touches the smaller circle.**

**__Additional Information__**

Chord Length in Concentric Circles

The length of the chord of the larger circle (radius R) that is tangent to the smaller circle (radius r) is given by 2 × √(R² − r²).

Tangent-Radius Theorem

A line is a tangent to a circle if and only if it is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of tangency.

Perpendicular Bisector

The perpendicular bisector of any chord of a circle always passes through the center of that circle.</p

questions.question: How does the volume of a sphere change when its radius is doubled?

The volume of a sphere (V) is directly proportional to the cube of its radius (r).

Relation: V ∝ r³

When the radius is doubled, the new radius becomes 2 × r.

Change in volume = (2)³ = 8 times.

**∴ The correct answer is Eight times.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial radius of the sphere = r

New radius of the sphere = 2r

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = (4/3) × π × (2r)³

⇒ V₂ = (4/3) × π × 8r³

⇒ V₂ = 8 × [(4/3) × π × r³]

⇒ V₂ = 8 × V₁

**∴ The correct answer is Eight times.**

**__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of a Sphere

The surface area (S) is given by 4 × π × r². If the radius is doubled, the surface area becomes 2² = 4 times.

Properties of a Hemisphere

Volume = (2/3) × π × r³ and Total Surface Area = 3 × π × r².

Ratio of Volumes

If the radii of two spheres are in the ratio a:b, then the ratio of their volumes is a³:b³.</p

questions.question: A triangle has sides of length 7 cm, 8 cm, and 9 cm. Find its perimeter.

 __Shortcut Trick__

Heron's Formula

Triangle Inequality Theorem

For any valid triangle, the sum of any two sides must always be strictly greater than the third side.</p

questions.question: A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter. The length of the rectangle is twice its width. If the side of the square is 12 meters, what is the difference between the area of the square and the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Perimeter of square = 12 × 4 = 48 m.

Rectangle perimeter ratio (L : W = 2 : 1) → 2 × (2 + 1) = 6 units.

6 units = 48 m → 1 unit = 8 m.

Dimensions of rectangle = 16 m and 8 m.

Difference in area = 12² − (16 × 8) = 144 − 128 = 16 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 16 m².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of square (s) = 12 m

Length of rectangle (L) = 2 × Width (W)

Perimeter of square = Perimeter of rectangle

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of square = 4 × side

Perimeter of rectangle = 2 × (length + width)

Area of square = side²

Area of rectangle = length × width

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff2feb77783b30b1686ab161b4cc8debf3ced8dc266671c240c443b714396979.png] 

⇒ Perimeter of square = 4 × 12 = 48 m

⇒ Perimeter of rectangle = 2(L + W) = 48 m

⇒ 2(2W + W) = 48

⇒ 6W = 48 → W = 8 m

⇒ L = 2 × 8 = 16 m

⇒ Area of square = 12² = 144 m²

⇒ Area of rectangle = 16 × 8 = 128 m²

⇒ Difference in area = 144 − 128 = 16 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 16 m².**

**__Additional Information__**

Maximum Area Property

For a fixed perimeter, a square always has a larger area than any other rectangle.

Perimeter and Side Relationship

If a square and rectangle have the same perimeter, the side of the square is the arithmetic mean of the rectangle dimensions: s = (L + W) ÷ 2.

Area Formulas

Area of Square = side² and Area of Rectangle = length × width. Units are always in square measure (m², cm², etc.).</p

questions.question: The average weight of 39 boys travelling to Ladakh is 30. If an fat boy with weight 130 kg join them. What will be the average weight of the group travelling to Ladakh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**32.5**__

 __Shortcut Trick__

Initial average of **39 boys** = **30**

Extra weight brought by **130 kg** boy = 130 − 30 = **100 kg**

Increase in average = Extra weight ÷ Total boys = 100 ÷ **40** = **2.5**

New average = 30 + 2.5 = **32.5**

**∴ The correct answer is 32.5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of boys = **39**, Initial average = **30**

Weight of new boy = **130 kg**

**Formula:**

**Average** = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5cbd437a116c342bd0d4b088283f1fcd9750d6b5f142d710015133e10cc7f1e8.png] 
⇒ Sum of weights of 39 boys = 39 × 30 = 1170 kg
⇒ Total weight including new boy = 1170 + 130 = 1300 kg
⇒ Total number of boys = 39 + 1 = 40
⇒ New average weight = 1300 ÷ 40 = **32.5**

**∴ The correct answer is 32.5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two groups are combined, the new average is Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Inclusion Rule

If a new member joins, New Average = Old Average + (Deviation ÷ New Strength).

Exclusion Rule

If a member leaves, New Average = Old Average − (Deviation ÷ New Strength).</p

questions.question: If P is 20% more than Q, and R is 20% less than Q, then P is what percentage more than R?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the **Ratio Method**:

P : Q = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5

R : Q = 80 : 100 = 4 : 5

Combining them, P : R = 6 : 4 = 3 : 2

P is more than R by (3 − 2) = 1 unit over base 2.

Required % = (1 / 2) × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P = Q + 20% of Q

R = Q − 20% of Q

**Formula Used:**

Percentage More = [(Value₁ − Value₂) / Value₂] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33eaa1eec38d5092f337fee447211b423a93e7534fc92fd375ceb8e8cb06fdcb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the value of **Q** be 100.

⇒ P = 100 + 20% of 100 = 100 + 20 = 120.

⇒ R = 100 − 20% of 100 = 100 − 20 = 80.

⇒ Difference between P and R = 120 − 80 = 40.

⇒ Required Percentage = (Difference / R) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (40 / 80) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 1/2 × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change Formula

The percentage change is calculated as [(Final Value − Initial Value) / Initial Value] × 100. Always identify the correct **base value** (the value after 'than').

Base Comparison Rule

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article at ₹1200 and offers a discount of 10%, but still makes a profit of 8%. What is the cost price?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Marked Price (MP)** = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 10) : (100 + 8) = 90 : 108 = 5 : 6

Given **MP** = 6 units = ₹1200 → 1 unit = ₹200

**CP** = 5 units = 5 × 200 = ₹1000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹1200, **Discount** = 10%, **Profit** = 8%

**Formula:** **Selling Price (SP)** = MP × (100 − D%)/100; **Cost Price (CP)** = SP × 100/(100 + P%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59b76565a7a0ada174a0c72a5c11de2fb0febef1cd50d685d1231f4e8d5abe9d.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price** = 1200 × (100 − 10) ÷ 100

⇒ **Selling Price** = 1200 × 90 ÷ 100 = ₹1080

⇒ **Cost Price** = 1080 × 100 ÷ (100 + 8)

⇒ **Cost Price** = 1080 × 100 ÷ 108 = ₹1000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

**Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Selling Price = MP − Discount.

Profit and Cost Price

**Profit** is calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**. Selling Price = CP + Profit.

CP and MP Relation

The ratio CP/MP = (100 − D%)/(100 + P%) is a direct result of equating the two expressions for **Selling Price**.

questions.question: If the ratio is 42 : 5 = 7x : 10. Then find the x.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given ratio: 42 : 5 = 7x : 10

Compare denominators: 10 is 5 × 2.

Therefore, compare numerators: 7x must be 42 × 2.

7x = 84 ⇒ x = 84 ÷ 7 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio 1 = 42 : 5

Ratio 2 = 7x : 10

Ratios are equal: 42 : 5 = 7x : 10

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43d806598ec4c3c39d0a59a74d21c33ecb4c7a92182ffac5f71cfad3f4cc9ebe.png] 

**Formula Used:**

If a : b = c : d, then a/b = c/d

Product of extremes = Product of means (a × d = b × c)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 42 ÷ 5 = 7x ÷ 10

⇒ 42 × 10 = 5 × 7x

⇒ 420 = 35x

⇒ x = 420 ÷ 35

⇒ x = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Proportion Rule

Four numbers a, b, c, d are in proportion if a : b = c : d, which implies a × d = b × c.

Fourth Proportional

If a : b = c : x, then x is the fourth proportional to a, b, and c, calculated as x = (b × c) ÷ a.

Simplifying Ratios

A ratio remains unchanged if both its terms are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero number.</p

questions.question: A man walks from A to B at 5 km/h and returns from B to A at 4 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When an equal distance is covered at two different speeds x and y, the average speed is given by the Harmonic Mean formula.

Average Speed = (2 × x × y) / (x + y)

Here, x = 5 km/h and y = 4 km/h.

Average Speed = (2 × 5 × 4) / (5 + 4) = 40 / 9 ≈ 4.44 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.4 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from A to B (v₁) = 5 km/h

Speed from B to A (v₂) = 4 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/63b236210c0e34ace998b5b7b30079153b8e23a0af206b05f52d977f31e69dee.png] 

⇒ Let the distance between A and B be 'd' km.

⇒ Time taken to go from A to B (t₁) = Distance ÷ Speed = d / 5 hours.

⇒ Time taken to return from B to A (t₂) = Distance ÷ Speed = d / 4 hours.

⇒ Total Distance for the whole journey = d + d = 2d km.

⇒ Total Time taken = t₁ + t₂ = d/5 + d/4 = (4d + 5d) / 20 = 9d / 20 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 2d ÷ (9d/20)

⇒ Average Speed = (2d × 20) / 9d = 40 / 9 km/h

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 4.44 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 4.4 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

If a person travels at speed v₁ for time t and speed v₂ for the same time t, the average speed is the Arithmetic Mean: (v₁ + v₂) / 2.

General Average Speed Formula

For any journey with different distances d₁, d₂ and speeds v₁, v₂, Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂) / (d₁/v₁ + d₂/v₂).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed = v₁ + v₂. In the same direction, relative speed = |v₁ − v₂|.
